proseFields.Red Flags:

The inverter and HV cabling look undisturbed in the photo, but a damaged HV battery, cooling circuit, or isolation fault would dramatically exceed the visible-panel repair cost — this is the dominant unquantifiable risk and must be checked before any bid.
- Cat S structural trigger not visible externally — chassis legs / crossmember behind the slam panel are the likely cause; confirm alignment.
- "Front Park Assist sensor failure" on the cluster confirms front sensor/harness damage from the impact.
- At least one front tyre is destroyed — confirm wheel/hub and suspension are not also damaged.
proseFields.Bidder Note: A near-new, very-low-mileage EV with a broad but mostly cosmetic/bolt-on front impact — attractive on paper, but the high-voltage system integrity behind the impact is the decisive unknown that could transform the economics. No previous salvage auction history — this appears to be a first write-off.

proseFields.Confidence Level: Medium — photos are clear and mileage is confirmed from the dash, but the EV high-voltage system condition cannot be verified from images.
proseFields.Key Cost Drivers:
- Full-width front impact requiring both headlamps, slam panel, cooling pack, bumper assembly and reinforcement bar — a broad parts list even though individual items are not premium.
- EV-specific risk: the impact is directly ahead of the high-voltage inverter and battery cooling circuit — diagnostics and HV integrity checks add cost and risk a much larger bill if HV components are compromised.
- The Cat S structural element (likely chassis leg / front crossmember behind the slam panel) needs proper assessment and possible jig work.
proseFields.Exit Band Position: mid — current-gen low-mileage EV (desirable), offset by full-width structural front impact and EV HV-system uncertainty.
proseFields.Margin Calculation: The repair is broad but composed largely of bolt-on front-end parts and a cosmetic rear quarter refinish, with the genuine wild card being the high-voltage system and chassis-leg structural work behind the slam panel. The desirability of a near-new top-trim EV supports a solid exit value, but the Cat S structural status, the EV stigma, and the unquantified HV risk keep the band position at mid rather than higher. The margin picture is favourable only if the HV system and structure prove sound on inspection — if they do not, the upper-bound repair cost rises sharply and the margin erodes. Confirm HV integrity before committing to a bid price.
proseFields.Recommended Action: Book a £10 Copart WhatsApp video inspection (minimum 48 hours before sale). This lot runs and drives with keys present, so confirmation of HV status and structural alignment is achievable remotely. Do not bid blind given the EV front-impact risk profile.
proseFields.Realistic Exit Value: This is a desirable vehicle on paper — a current-generation (2026) battery-electric compact SUV in top "Max Extended Range" trim with delivery-level mileage (2,681 miles). Near-delivery mileage on the current model generation normally pushes a vehicle toward the upper band even for an EV, as newness overrides battery-anxiety. However, this is a Cat S structural write-off with a full-width front impact directly ahead of the HV system, and the structural/heavy-damage signal pulls firmly back toward mid. The two signals — strong desirability versus heavy structural front damage with EV HV uncertainty — net out around the middle of the Cat S band. I am placing it mid.
proseFields.Visible Damage Summary:
Confirmed body style: 5-door Hatchback (compact SUV). This is a 2026 Citroën ë-C3 Aircross — a battery-electric vehicle (confirmed by the orange high-voltage cabling and silver power-electronics/inverter unit visible in the engine bay, the "Danger High Voltage" EV placards, and the DVLA-confirmed ELECTRICITY fuel type).

Windscreen sticker suffix: the lot sticker (53337506) shows an "X" suffix — insurance company vendor (lower value category). Vendor type confirmed as insurer-entered.

Category: Cat S (Repairable Structural) — confirmed in listing data.

The primary damage is a full-width front-end impact. The front bumper, bumper reinforcement bar, grille, lower air dam/undertray, slam panel/front carrier, and both front lamp assemblies are displaced or removed across the entire front of the vehicle. The bonnet leading edge is lifted/displaced. Looking into the exposed bay, the radiator/condenser pack and cooling components are exposed; the high-voltage inverter and HV cabling sit behind and appear undisturbed in the photo, but their condition cannot be confirmed from images. The front crash bar (painted gold/primer) is visible and appears deformed.

Front lamp status: both front headlamps are dislodged/hanging from their mountings with the bumper removed and apertures fully exposed — serviceability cannot be confirmed; on a full-width front impact both lamps are implicated.

At least one front tyre is severely degraded — shredded/delaminated down to the sidewall structure (front tyre on the damaged corner; the opposite-side front shows mud/contamination). Front tyre damage is consistent with being driven flat or with kerb/impact damage — corner-level certainty is limited but at least one front tyre is destroyed.

Rear/side: there is light cosmetic damage on the rear quarter area near the rear lamp — scuffs and light scratching to the rear quarter panel paint and the charge-port/vent moulding (the black mesh insert in the quarter appears cracked/displaced in the close-up). The rear lamp cluster glass appears intact. This is non-impact-grade cosmetic marking consistent with the "Minor Dents/Scratches" secondary descriptor.

Dashboard: cluster reads READY with "D" engaged and a "Front Park Assist sensor failure" message plus several amber/red telltales — consistent with front sensors/wiring damaged in the impact. Odometer reads 2,681 miles in the dash photo, matching the listing figure exactly.

Interior front and rear: clean, undamaged, no airbag deployment visible — steering wheel centre and dash fascia intact.
proseFields.Alternative Damage Scenario: The damage fully matches the description — a genuine front-end collision. The single prior salvage record (10 Jun 2026, same Cat S, same 2,681 miles, same Front End damage) is this lot's own database entry echoing back, not a separate prior auction event — there is no genuine prior history here.
proseFields.WhatsApp Inspection Checklist:
1. Confirm the high-voltage system status — ask whether the dash shows READY without HV/isolation fault warnings, and whether any HV service/diagnostic messages are present; show the inverter and HV cabling close up for any crush or chafe damage.
2. Show the front chassis legs / crossmember from below for deformation or misalignment — this is the likely Cat S structural trigger behind the slam panel.
3. Confirm both front wheels sit straight in the arches and show the destroyed-side front wheel, hub and suspension close up for impact damage.
4. Show the radiator/condenser cooling pack and both front lamp mountings close up to confirm extent of damage and whether the lamps are reusable.
5. Confirm the bonnet, both front doors and tailgate open and close correctly and that panel gaps are even (structural sanity check).
6. Confirm the "Front Park Assist sensor failure" is the only fault and show the full cluster for any additional warning lights on the running vehicle.
7. Inspect the opposite-side front headlamp — on a full-width frontal impact both lamps are implicated; check for displacement, cracking, or moisture ingress and confirm serviceability. Budget ~£350 if replacement needed — flagged as inspection allowance, not included in repair total.
8. Inspect and photograph all four wheels and tyres close-up — confirm no shredding, kerbing, cuts or bulges (the listing photos do not show the wheels clearly enough to confirm condition)
